# BrickWorth

> BrickWorth is an app that finds out what your brick sets are worth. Take a photo of a set box, a built model or an instruction booklet, and BrickWorth identifies the set (number, name, year, piece count, minifigures with photos, retired or not) and shows its retail price and an estimated value as sealed, built complete or used and loose. Add sets to your shelf to track your collection's value over time against what you paid.

BrickWorth: Brick Set Scanner — Minifig Collector & Value. iPhone app, available on the App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6780850054?pt=128855456&ct=ai_web

## Guides

- [How to Find Out What Your Brick Sets Are Worth on iPhone](https://qwerpap.github.io/brickworth-legal/best-app-to-find-out-what-your-brick-sets-are-worth): Photograph the set box in BrickWorth, or type the set number.
- [How to Check the Value of a Retired Brick Set on iPhone](https://qwerpap.github.io/brickworth-legal/check-value-of-retired-brick-set): Search the set in BrickWorth by number or name.
- [How to Identify a Brick Set From a Photo on iPhone](https://qwerpap.github.io/brickworth-legal/identify-brick-set-from-photo): Photograph the box, the built model or the instruction booklet in BrickWorth and it returns the set number, name, year, piece count and minifigures.
- [How to Scan a Brick Set Box and See Its Price on iPhone](https://qwerpap.github.io/brickworth-legal/scan-brick-box-price-app): Open BrickWorth, tap Scan a set and photograph the front of the box.
- [How to Track the Value of Your Brick Collection on iPhone](https://qwerpap.github.io/brickworth-legal/track-brick-collection-value): Add each set to your BrickWorth shelf and it totals the estimated value of your collection, shows how it changed over time and compares it with what you…
